note: Proposed NEW JFR events derived from gap analysis of -Xlog log sites that no existing JFR event covers. These events DO NOT exist in the JDK 25 oracle (jfr metadata, 194 events); they are candidates for upstream proposal. Scope of this analysis: -Xlog:trimnative*,gc*,gc+region*,gc+ergo*,gc+humongous*,stringdedup*=info (127 uncovered firing sites). Each 'replaces' entry cites the HotSpot source file + verbatim log format string the event would make recoverable via JFR. Field types follow the oracle convention (long for time/bytes/counters, int for ids, float/double for ratios, boolean/String). startTime/duration follow the standard JFR event contract. Status note (2026-08-17): JDK 26 adds jdk.StringDeduplication (byte-level fields included — our proposed StringDeduplicationStatistics is now REDUNDANT; see rationale). JDK 27 adds jdk.ShenandoahPromotionInformation (in metadata.xml, not yet released). JDK-8365306 (NativeHeapTrim JFR, PR #26756, closed 2025-12): PR was blocked on ProcessSize umbrella design — a narrow trim-only re-proposal would likely be accepted per Erik Gahlin. G1 now has UseGCOverheadLimit (JDK-8212084, merged JDK 26, PR #27950) but no JFR event. JEP 521 Generational Shenandoah became production-ready in JDK 25 (merged May 2025). None of the other 10 proposed events have upstream work in progress. Critique pass 3 applied 2026-08-17: G1 log format strings corrected from source (print_refinement_stats starts with 'Refinement took', not 'Concurrent refinement'); ZDirectorRule missing fields added (gcCPUTime, gcWorkers, acceptableGCInterval, timeSinceLastGC, freePercent, interval, proactiveEnabled); ZNMethodRegistration tableRebuilt noted as needing new instrumentation; ShenandoahCardStatistics spurious dirtyObjs field removed (#ifndef PRODUCT guard noted); ShenandoahMMU gcId added, periodic-sample path noted; ShenandoahReclaimProgress early-exit semantics corrected (fields 2-4 nullable); PSAdaptiveSizePolicy minMutatorIntervalSec removed (does not exist), desiredEdenDelta semantics fixed, pauseMs renamed to minorPauseMs; NativeHeapTrim deltaBytes corrected to signed long; StringDeduplicationStatistics marked redundant.

proposed.label: Shenandoah Card Statistics
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah generational (only, JEP 521 production-ready in JDK 25) remembered-set card scanning emits cumulative dirty/clean card statistics per GC cycle with no JFR event. IMPORTANT: the log() method is wrapped in #ifndef PRODUCT — this event would only fire in debug/fastdebug builds unless the JFR emission point is moved to a product-build path. The per-worker stats are gated behind ShenandoahEnableCardStats (non-product); this event emits only the cumulative aggregate. dirtyScannedObjects maps to _dirty_scan_obj_cnt — the count of heap objects visited as a result of dirty card scans (distinct from dirtyCards = card-table slot count). The _alternation_cnt field (consecutive dirty/clean alternation count, a cache-efficiency indicator) is available in the class but not in the primary log line; could be added. maxConsecutiveDirtyCards reflects card-table clustering that affects scan efficiency.

proposed.label: Shenandoah Minimum Mutator Utilization
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah's MMU tracker prints GC utilization (GCU) and mutator utilization (MU) per completed phase with no JFR analogue. Not redundant with jdk.GCCPUTime: GCCPUTime gives raw user/sys/real CPU slices; this gives normalized MU% over the phase window. Low muPercent directly indicates mutator starvation — a production-critical signal. There are TWO distinct emission paths: (1) update_utilization() at end of each GC cycle — phase is one of 'Concurrent Young GC', 'Concurrent Global GC', 'Concurrent Bootstrap GC', 'Mixed Concurrent GC', 'Full GC', 'Degenerated GC'; periodSeconds = gc_cycle_period; (2) report() periodic-sample path (every ~5s default) — phase would be absent/null; periodSeconds = time_delta since last sample. These paths should ideally be separate events or distinguished by an isPeriodicSample boolean. gcId must be included for correlation with jdk.GarbageCollection and other GC events (source: _most_recent_gcid tracked in ShenandoahMmuTracker).

proposed.label: Shenandoah Reclaim Progress
proposed.rationale: shenandoahMetrics.cpp's is_good_progress() evaluates four independent dimensions after each cycle. IMPORTANT early-exit semantics: the function returns on the FIRST dimension that passes (or after free-space fails). This means not all 4 dimensions are logged every cycle. Typical paths: (a) only free-space logged if free-space check fails immediately; (b) free-space + used-space logged if free-space passes but used-space also passes early; etc. Fields for dimensions 2-4 are NULLABLE — they may not be populated on a given invocation. A consumer must handle null/absent values. Fragmentation values are fractions (0.0-1.0) in source (_if_before - current_if computes the delta); the log multiplies by 100 before printing. Store as percentage (0.0-100.0) for usability. freeNeeded = (softMaxCapacity/100) * ShenandoahCriticalFreeThreshold (bytes). usedNeededToFree = ShenandoahHeapRegion::region_size_bytes() — effectively a fixed constant, included for self-containedness. goodProgress=false in any dimension signals risk of degenerated GC fallback. consecutiveDegenWithoutProgress (from ShenandoahCollectorPolicy._consecutive_degenerated_gcs_without_progress) is a high-value diagnostic missing from this event — consider adding.

proposed.label: ZGC NMethod Registration
proposed.rationale: ZGC requires all nmethods to have load barriers patched (registered). The NMethod table tracks live registrations and cumulative unregistrations. High unregistered counts can indicate classloader churn or code cache pressure. Field semantics from ZNMethodTable.cpp: registeredNMethods = _nregistered (current live count); staleNMethodSlots = _nunregistered (entries unregistered but not yet pruned from hash table — NOT a cumulative total since JVM start). tableRebuilt: DESIGN GAP — no per-cycle tableRebuilt boolean exists in ZStatNMethods::print() which only reads _nregistered/_nunregistered. A rebuild is detectable via a debug-level log in ZNMethodTable::rebuild() but is a separate code path. To make tableRebuilt accurate, ZNMethodTable would need a new atomic counter read at stat time — this requires new instrumentation beyond the existing log. The ZNMethodTable rebuild triggers (shrink/grow/prune thresholds) and old/new table sizes are logged in rebuild() at debug level; a dedicated jdk.ZNMethodTableRebuild event would be more appropriate. Production validation: low — no external evidence found that nmethod table overhead is a common production problem. Recommend de-prioritizing this event.

proposed.label: GC Overhead Limit Exceeded
proposed.rationale: Fires immediately before the JVM throws OutOfMemoryError: GC Overhead Limit exceeded. Now implemented in both G1 (JDK-8212084, merged JDK 26 PR #27950) and Parallel GC. The three diagnostic fields make the event self-contained — without them a consumer cannot tell whether the OOM was time-driven or space-driven. IMPORTANT: Parallel GC logs TWO separate free-space values (young + old gen), while G1 logs one combined value. The event must handle both: include freeSpaceYoungPercent and freeSpaceOldPercent for Parallel (both null for G1). gcTimePercent: G1 uses long_term_gc_time_ratio()*100; Parallel uses 100-mutator_time_percent(). Both are 0-100 percentages. consecutiveViolations = _gc_overhead_counter (increments on each consecutive violating GC, resets to zero on a clean GC — it is the counter, not the threshold; threshold is GCOverheadLimitThreshold flag, default 5). collector field distinguishes G1 from Parallel since free-space field population differs. gcId is GCId::peek() — last completed GC id (approximate, not an active GC).

proposed.label: Native Heap Trim
proposed.rationale: The JVM periodically calls malloc_trim/madvise to return RSS to the OS after GC (NativeHeapTrimmer thread, -XX:TrimNativeHeapInterval). The log line records before/after RSS and delta, but no JFR event carries this. Especially valuable on containerised deployments where RSS spikes are monitored closely. detailsAvailable=false when /proc/self/status is unavailable (non-Linux or restricted containers). JDK-8365306 (PR #26756) was closed 2025-12 due to design dispute about a ProcessSize umbrella event — the NativeHeapTrim event itself was not objected to by Erik Gahlin; a narrow trim-only re-proposal is recommended. deltaBytes: CORRECTED from previous design — the source computes an unsigned delta plus a sign char; deltaBytes should be a signed long (afterBytes - beforeBytes); negative = RSS reduced (trimmed), positive = RSS grew. trimCount = _num_trims_performed (uint64_t, incremented before logging, so first trim = 1, cumulative since JVM start).

proposed.label: G1 Concurrent Refinement Sweep
proposed.rationale: G1 concurrent refinement sweeps the dirty-card queue (DCQS) between pauses. This event fires once per sweep (potentially multiple times per GC pause). CORRECTED log format: print_refinement_stats() STARTS WITH 'Refinement took %.2fms' not 'Concurrent refinement: wanted'. The 'wanted' / 'pendingFromGC' fields were incorrect — they come from adjust_threads_wanted() in g1ConcurrentRefine.cpp (a separate function). The actual log has: total duration, pre-sweep and card-refine sub-durations, and 8 card categories. cardsNoCrossRegion = no_cross_region (within-region references filtered early, high value = good heap locality). The JDK 25 write barrier redesign (JEP 522) changed refinement behavior significantly — this event is needed to understand the new refinement dynamics. Counterpart jdk.G1ConcurrentRefinementPolicy fires from g1Policy.cpp record_young_collection_end() and adjust_threads_wanted() separately.

proposed.label: G1 Concurrent Refinement Policy Update
proposed.rationale: Fires once per young-GC pause. CORRECTED: the claimed format string 'Concurrent refinement: wanted %u, pending cards target %zu, predicted refine rate %.2f...' does not exist verbatim. The actual sources are THREE separate log statements: (1) g1Policy.cpp record_young_collection_end() logs 'GC refinement: goal: %zu / %1.2fms, actual: %zu / %1.2fms, %s' with pendingCardsTarget, goalMs, pendingCards, actualMs, exceededGoalSuffix; (2) g1ConcurrentRefine.cpp adjust_threads_wanted() logs wanted + predicted + goal + rates; (3) separate refine/dirty rate logs. A JFR event would naturally aggregate these at the pause boundary. threadsWanted and pendingCardsFromGC come from adjust_threads_wanted() in g1ConcurrentRefine.cpp (not g1Policy.cpp). predictedRefineRate comes from record_refinement_stats(). predictedPendingCards (not in original proposal) is logged by adjust_threads_wanted() alongside threadsWanted. exceededGoal is modeled as boolean (source: string suffix ' (exceeded goal)' vs empty). The pending card target and goal window are the primary levers for diagnosing whether adaptive refinement keeps up with write-barrier pressure.

proposed.label: ZGC Director Rule Evaluation
proposed.rationale: ZGC's director evaluates rules to decide whether to trigger GC. The gc+director log tag records each rule evaluation with context data. IMPORTANT design notes from source analysis: (1) Early-exit: make_minor_gc_decision and make_major_gc_decision return on first triggered rule — at most one Minor and one Major rule fires per cycle. (2) rule_minor_allocation_rate_static (UseDynamicNumberOfGCThreads=false) is a separate variant with NO gcCPUTime/gcWorkers/allocRateVariancePct fields. (3) Proactive rule has TWO mutually exclusive branches: enabled (AcceptableGCInterval/TimeSinceLastGC/TimeUntilGC) vs not-yet-enabled (UsedUntilEnabled/TimeUntilEnabled — logs but does not trigger). (4) rule_major_allocation_rate is an ESCALATION rule called from start_gc() (not make_major_gc_decision) — it upgrades a minor decision to major; ExtraYoungGCTimeForLookahead is in the log but was missing from the original proposal. (5) Timer rule applies to both generations (rule_minor_timer + rule_major_timer) with Interval field in log. (6) High Usage log has freePercent that was missing. (7) GCCPUTime and GCWorkers were missing from the dynamic AllocationRate rule. Soft/semi-hard/hard sub-variants of the dynamic allocation rate rule share the same log format — the triggering variant is not distinguishable from the log alone.

proposed.label: Parallel GC Adaptive Size Policy
proposed.rationale: Parallel GC's AdaptiveSizePolicy runs a feedback loop after each GC to resize eden and survivor toward throughput and pause-time goals. CORRECTED fields from source analysis: (1) minMutatorIntervalSec REMOVED — does not exist; MinGCDistanceSecond is a compile-time constant, not a stored instance field. (2) desiredEdenDelta CORRECTED — only logged on throughput-increase branch inside compute_desired_eden_size(), always positive (never negative), branch-conditional; renamed to throughputEdenIncrease and noted as branch-specific. (3) pauseMs renamed to minorPauseMs — source is minor_gc_time_estimate() only; major GC tracked separately and not in print_stats(). (4) mutatorIntervalSec/Last renamed to gcDistanceSec/Last — source variable is _gc_distance_seconds_seq ('gc-distance' in log). (5) throughputGoal: no stored field; re-derived as calculate_throughput_goal(GCTimeRatio) at emission time. (6) desiredEden/Survivor: not emittable from print_stats() — requires caller site in psYoungGen.cpp. (7) promotedBytesEstimate/Last are floating-point doubles in source, not integer bytes. Field notes: survivorOverflow is softer than PromotionFailed — some objects bypass survivor to old gen. shrinkBytes from compute_old_gen_shrink_bytes() uses 10-min promotion rate lookahead.

proposed.label: Shenandoah Collection Decision
proposed.rationale: Shenandoah generational mode's regulator/control FSM decides each cycle what to collect. CORRECTED fields from source analysis: (1) immediateGarbagePercent REMOVED — does not exist in any source file; source uses immediate_garbage (bytes) and immediate_regions (count) in shenandoahOldHeuristics.cpp. (2) decision field: no enum/string constant; GCMode enum values are: none, concurrent_normal, stw_degenerated, stw_full, servicing_old, bootstrapping_old, stopped (shenandoahGenerationalControlThread.hpp). The decision must be synthesized from which regulator code path fired; use String type with documented values. (3) generation: C++ object pointer in source; must be mapped to String ('Young'/'Old'/'Global'). (4) oldEvacuationBudget: byte count (_old_evacuation_budget), confirmed as long type. (5) This event spans MULTIPLE code sites — no single function emits all fields simultaneously; JFR implementation requires instrumentation at 3+ call sites. (6) available and softMaxCapacity must be captured at heuristic evaluation time. High-value for generational Shenandoah production operators — understanding why global (expensive) vs young-only cycles are chosen is critical.
